subject: general
question: Pipe P can fill (3)/(4) part of a tank in 15 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(6) part of the same tank in 25 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 2 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 5 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time for P to fill tank = 15 × 4/3 = 20 h, and Q = 25 × 6/5 = 30 h.

Let Total Work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.

Efficiency: P = 3 units/h, Q = 2 units/h. Filled in 2 hrs = (3 + 2) × 2 = 10 units.

Pipe R empties 10 units in 5 hrs ⇒ Efficiency of R = −2 units/h.

Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 3 + 2 − 2 = 3 units/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to fill 3/4 part = 15 hours

⇒ Time for P to fill the full tank = 15 × 4/3 = 20 hours

Time taken by Q to fill 5/6 part = 25 hours

⇒ Time for Q to fill the full tank = 25 × 6/5 = 30 hours

Part of tank filled by P and Q in 2 hours = 2 × (1/20 + 1/30) = 2 × (3 + 2)/60 = 1/6

Pipe R empties this 1/6 part in 5 hours.

⇒ Time for R to empty the full tank = 5 × 6 = 30 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 3 + 2 − 2 = 3 units/hr

⇒ Time taken by P, Q, and R together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and its work is considered positive (+). An outlet or emptying pipe drains the tank, so its work is considered negative (−).

Total Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is the amount of work done in a unit time. It is inversely proportional to the time taken. Total Work = Time Taken × Combined Efficiency.

Work Cycle Principle

If pipes operate on alternate hours, the total work is divided by the work done in one complete cycle to find the number of cycles needed.
